events.summary: Solid first cut with good sourcing from FNPS, UF/IFAS, Florida Wildflower Foundation, NC State Extension, and NCBI/StatPearls. High confidence on native status, butterfly host, wildlife, growing conditions, and Ayurvedic history. Moderate confidence on edibility/toxicity color calls — sources are split on pet safety (UF/IFAS says non-toxic; one informal site conflates it with a different 'herb of grace'); I've stayed with the UF/IFAS and veterinary consensus of non-toxic but noted GI caution at quantity.

events.feedback:
Here is a deep-dive audit for the Herb-of-Grace (Bacopa monnieri) draft page:

🔍 Botanical & Ecological Accuracy
Taxonomy & Native Status: Spot on. Bacopa monnieri (Plantaginaceae) is correctly flagged as native across Florida (FNPS / Atlas of Florida Plants) with a broad pantropical distribution.

Ayurvedic / Medicinal Context: Highlighting its history as Brahmi and the role of bacosides adds great narrative depth while keeping clinical claims appropriately measured.

Wildlife Interactions:

Accurately details its role as a larval host for the White Peacock butterfly (Anartia jatrophae).

Correctly notes its value as a nearly year-round nectar source in Southwest Florida.

Distinction Note: The warning under NOTES distinguishing native Bacopa monnieri from nursery Sutera cordata (often sold under the trade name "Bacopa") is a high-value inclusion for home gardeners.
